subject: Contract synchronicity checklist and close-path dependencies
messages:
From: Sasha Park <sasha@biocorp.io>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ellen Cho <ellen.cho@biocorp.io>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract synchronicity checklist and close-path dependencies

Markus / Laura —

Thanks for sending over the draft and the high-level timeline. Legal at Biocorp ran a quick pass and surfaced two items that will affect procurement sequencing:

- Data residency clause (section 6): needs explicit EU-processing carveout for our EU customers — this may require an additional DPA exhibit.
- SLA credit language (section 9.3): procurement insists on a 45-day cure period before credits — procurement wants this aligned to our internal billing cycles.

We can turn this around quickly if Redwood can confirm:
1) Whether the DPA exhibit is acceptable and where it will be attached (order form vs separate amendment).
2) A single source of truth for signature flow: is DocuSign initiated from Redwood or will Biocorp route?

I attached our redlines for quick reference.

Attachment: redlines_biocorp.pdf (pdf, 427 KB)

Best,
Sasha
Sasha Park
Head of Procurement, Biocorp Therapeutics
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sasha Park <sasha@biocorp.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract synchronicity checklist and close-path dependencies

Sasha —

Appreciate the speedy review and the redlines. Short answers up front:
- DPA exhibit: Redwood prefers attaching the DPA as an exhibit on the order form to keep the MSA lean, but we can accommodate a separate amendment if Biocorp legal requires it.
- DocuSign flow: we can initiate from our account and send to Biocorp, or we can accept a Biocorp-initiated envelope — whichever you prefer operationally.

Immediate ask: can you let us know which approach Biocorp legal favors by EOD Wednesday (5/27)? That decision will determine whether procurement needs an internal approval for an amendment vs. an exhibit — which affects their sign-off path.

Next steps I propose from Redwood:
- Internal alignment doc: attached a checklist with proposed owners and estimated lead times per item.
- One short alignment call with Biocorp legal + procurement to lock the attachment approach and signature flow. 20 minutes should do it.

Attachment: close_timeline_checklist.xlsx (xlsx, 68 KB)

Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: Ellen Cho <ellen.cho@biocorp.io>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sasha Park <sasha@biocorp.io>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2026 14:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract synchronicity checklist and close-path dependencies

Thanks Markus — quick clarifications from legal: we prefer the DPA as a separate exhibit rather than embedding too many obligations in the MSA. That keeps our procurement record clearer.

Operationally:
- If the DPA is a separate exhibit, procurement will treat that as an "amendment package" and will require an internal sign-off from our CISO and Privacy Officer. That adds ~5 business days.
- DocuSign: Biocorp prefers Redwood to originate the envelope so we can get the right signing order into the system.

Given that, our tentative impact on the close timeline: add 5 business days for legal+privacy approvals if the DPA is separate. If you can convert to an exhibit attached to the order form, we can compress that to 1-2 days.

Ellen
Ellen Cho
Legal Operations, Biocorp Therapeutics
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sasha Park <sasha@biocorp.io>, Ellen Cho <ellen.cho@biocorp.io>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2026 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract synchronicity checklist and close-path dependencies

Team —

Biocorp legal prefers a separate DPA exhibit and wants Redwood to originate the DocuSign envelope. That pushes us toward a 5-business-day delta unless we change the attachment approach. Action items for Redwood to avoid slipping the target close (target signature week of June 7):

- Karthik: Please review the attached contract_draft_v3.docx and prepare a redline that keeps the DPA as an exhibit but offers a short play: a one-paragraph exhibit summary inside the order form that references the full DPA. Estimate: 24 hours.
- Vanessa: Coordinate with finance/billing to confirm whether our billing cycle alignment can accept a 45-day cure period; if not, propose alternative wording that procurement can accept without requiring a billing-team exception. Estimate: 48 hours.
- Laura: Prepare the DocuSign envelope template we will use (signing order: Redwood legal -> Biocorp legal -> Biocorp CFO) and flag any fields that need pre-population. Estimate: EOD Friday.

If we hit these timelines we should preserve our target without executive escalation. If any item slips, we'll need to brief the customer success lead and consider a one-week extension.

Attachment: contract_draft_v3.docx (docx, 112 KB)

-Markus

Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract synchronicity checklist and close-path dependencies

Markus / team —

Quick update from legal review (redline attached):
- Inserted a one-paragraph exhibit summary into the order form that references the full DPA (we kept the DPA as a separate exhibit per Biocorp request).
- Tightened SLA credit language to align with billing: added language that a 45-day cure period is tracked from invoice generation and that credits are applied on the next billing cycle. This should remove the need for a billing-team exception.
- Added a small change to the signature block to support Redwood-originated DocuSign envelopes (ensures proper signer order).

If Biocorp is OK with the combined approach (separate DPA exhibit + order-form summary + Redwood-originated envelope), Ellen's estimated 5-business-day path will likely become 1-2 days.

Attachment: redline_contract_draft_v3.docx (docx, 92 KB)

Vanessa — any blockers on the billing adjustment?

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
